text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Mobil Oil Corp of the United States has entered into partnership with the Army Welfare Trusupport of the Kenyan authorities in checking tea smuggling from there.
- Pakistan is studying a report which may f capital value tax on international air-tickets, immovable property and motor vehicles.
- Pakistan's $1.6 billion Hub power project will be completed ahead of schedule, Hub Power Co Ltd (HUBCO) chief executive Michael Woodroffe said.

- National security concerns, with special reference to the current situation in Afghanistan and elections in Indian-held Kashmir, were discussed by President Farooq Leghari, Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto and Army Chief of Staff General Jahangir Karamat at a meeting in Islamabad.
- The 52-member Organisation of the Islamic Conference will send a mission to Afghanistan to urge an end to fighting.
- At least 10,000 Afghans have fled to Pakistan since the capture of Kabul by Taleban militia, a U.N. official said.
- A convoy of 20 trucks will leave Islamabad on October 21 to usher in transit trade traffic between Pakistan and China and some Central Asian states.
- The cabinet has approved recovery of 1.3 billion rupees outstanding dues of the Water and Power Development authority and Karachi Electric Supply Corporation.
- The government is preparing modalities of imposing agricultural income tax in Pakistan and is likely to take up the matter in parliament.
- Opposition leader Nawaz Sharif asked the government to get parliamentary approval before imposing any new taxes.
- Chinese President Jiang Xi Min is scheduled to pay a bilateral visit to Pakistan in December.
